prose.text: The Private Access authentication Settings page holds a handful of tenant-wide authentication options. {{enforce-sso}}

prose.label: Browser behavior.

prose.label: Private Service Edge outage.
prose.text: {{max-age-pse}} This is a different field from the Disaster Recovery Mode max age in [[zpa.private-service-edges.disaster-recovery:max-age-for-authentication]]. Which feature the limited-availability note covers, and how the setting interacts with timeout policy, is open {{gap:max-age-open}}.

checks.do: Whether Enforce SSO Login for Admins is on, which stops local admin login except for the default admin account Zscaler created.
Whether the NameID's domain suffix matches the primary or a secondary authentication domain, which only Zscaler Support can change for the primary.
Which max-age field a question is about, this page's Private Service Edge setting or the Disaster Recovery Mode one, since the defaults differ.

enforce-sso.statement: Enforce SSO Login for Admins forces Private Access admins to log in to the Admin Console using SSO only, and requires admin SSO to be enabled in an IdP configuration; admins cannot then log in locally. The default admin account Zscaler created for the organization (zpaadmin@<domain>.com or admin@<domain>.com) can still log in locally.

quotes: Enforce SSO Login for Admins: Enable to force Private Access admins to log into the Zscaler Admin Console using single sign-on (SSO) only. If you enable this setting, you must also enable admin SSO in an IdP configuration.
When enabled, admins can't log in locally.

If this setting is enabled, the default admin account that was initially created for your organization by Zscaler (i.e., zpaadmin@<your organization's domain>.com or admin@<your organization's domain>.com) can still log in locally.

cors.statement: CORS Request, when enabled, allows cross-origin resource sharing to request access to selected resources from a different origin; the setting defaults to Disabled.

quotes: CORS Request: Enable to allow CORS (cross-origin resource sharing) to request access to selected resources from a different origin, other than its own.
permitting access to the response if they match. By default, this is set to Disabled.

samesite.statement: SameSite Cookie Attribute, when enabled, sets the SameSite attribute of application domain cookies and authentication domain cookies to None for all Browser Access applications; it defaults to Disabled.

quotes: SameSite Cookie Attribute: Enable to set the SameSite cookie attribute for application domain cookies and authentication domain cookies to None for all Browser Access applications. By default, this is set to Disabled.

session-timeout.statement: Admin Portal Session Timeout (In Minutes) specifies how long admins can be inactive on the Admin Console before logout; the default is 30 minutes and any interval from 5 to 600 minutes can be entered. A confirmation window appears 5 minutes before logout asking whether to extend the session.

quotes: Admin Portal Session Timeout (In Minutes): This specifies how long admins can be inactive on the Zscaler Admin Console before they are logged out.

The default value is 30 minutes, but you can enter any time interval from 5 to 600 minutes. A confirmation window appears 5 minutes before an admin is logged out, asking if they want to extend their session.

authentication-domains.statement: Zscaler Support updates the Primary Authentication Domain. During authentication the domain suffix in the NameID must match that domain or a Secondary Authentication Domain, the other domains owned by the organization. The authentication domains have no relationship to application domains, but they can overlap.

quotes: Primary Authentication Domain: The primary domain your organization uses for authentication. Contact Zscaler Support to update this field.
During authentication, the domain suffix in the NameID must match this domain or the domains listed in Secondary Authentication Domains.
Secondary Authentication Domains: These are other domains owned by your organization, but not configured as the primary authentication domain.
The primary and secondary authentication domains have no relationship to application domains, but they can overlap.

max-age-pse.statement: Max Age for Authentication with Private Service Edge specifies how long a user's authentication is extended when the Private Service Edge cannot communicate with the Private Access cloud during a customer's network outage, measured since the last authentication. The maximum is 7 days and the default is 0 Days; the page says this feature and its procedures are in limited availability.

quotes: Max Age for Authentication with Private Service Edge: This specifies the duration that the user's authentication is extended when the Private Service Edge for Private Access cannot communicate to the Private Access cloud during a customer's network outage.
This allows users to connect to Private Service Edges and access applications for the specified duration since the last time you authenticated.
The maximum allowed limit for the duration is 7 days.
By default, this is set to 0 Days.
This feature and its procedures are in limited availability.

cors-samesite-effect.title: What SameSite None and the CORS Request switch change for Browser Access in practice
cors-samesite-effect.detail: The page states what each switch sets and its default, not the effect on Browser Access sessions or which resources CORS covers.

max-age-open.title: Scope of the limited-availability note and the interaction of Max Age with timeout policy
max-age-open.detail: The page follows the Max Age setting with a limited-availability note without saying which feature it covers, and does not say how the setting interacts with timeout policy; the Disaster Recovery page gives a recommendation for its own field only.
